name: Shape
brief: A class representing two-dimensional figures and their properties.
description: A shape has three major properties: shape outline, stroking, filling. The outline in the Shape is retained as the path. Path can be composed by accumulating primitive commands such as moveTo(), lineTo(), cubicTo(), or complete shape interfaces such as appendRect(), appendCircle(), etc. Path can consists of sub-paths. One sub-path is determined by a close command.

The stroke of Shape is an optional property in case the Shape needs to be represented with/without the outline borders. It's efficient since the shape path and the stroking path can be shared with each other. It's also convenient when controlling both in one context.
warnings: This class is not designed for inheritance.

members.name: reset
members.brief: Resets the shape path.
description: The transformation matrix, color, fill, and stroke properties are retained.
notes: The memory where the path data is stored is not deallocated at this stage to allow for caching.

members.name: moveTo
members.signature: Result moveTo(float x, float y) noexcept
members.brief: Sets the initial point of the sub-path.
description: The value of the current point is set to the given point.

params.name: x
params.description: The horizontal coordinate of the initial point of the sub-path.

params.name: y
params.description: The vertical coordinate of the initial point of the sub-path.

members.name: lineTo
members.signature: Result lineTo(float x, float y) noexcept
members.brief: Adds a new point to the sub-path, which results in drawing a line from the current point to the given end-point.
description: The value of the current point is set to the given end-point.

params.name: x
params.description: The horizontal coordinate of the end-point of the line.

params.name: y
params.description: The vertical coordinate of the end-point of the line.

notes: In case this is the first command in the path, it corresponds to the moveTo() call.

members.name: cubicTo
members.signature: Result cubicTo(float cx1, float cy1, float cx2, float cy2, float x, float y) noexcept
members.brief: Adds new points to the sub-path, which results in drawing a cubic Bezier curve starting at the current point and ending at the given end-point (`x`, `y`) using the control points (`cx1`, `cy1`) and (`cx2`, `cy2`).
description: The value of the current point is set to the given end-point.

params.name: cx1
params.description: The horizontal coordinate of the 1st control point.

params.name: cy1
params.description: The vertical coordinate of the 1st control point.

params.name: cx2
params.description: The horizontal coordinate of the 2nd control point.

params.name: cy2
params.description: The vertical coordinate of the 2nd control point.

params.name: x
params.description: The horizontal coordinate of the end-point of the curve.

params.name: y
params.description: The vertical coordinate of the end-point of the curve.

warnings: cubicTo must not be the first command in the path. Otherwise, rendering is not guaranteed.

members.name: close
members.brief: Closes the current sub-path by drawing a line from the current point to the initial point of the sub-path.
description: The value of the current point is set to the initial point of the closed sub-path.
notes: In case the sub-path does not contain any points, this function has no effect.

members.name: appendRect
members.signature: Result appendRect(float x, float y, float w, float h, float rx = 0, float ry = 0, bool cw = true) noexcept
members.brief: Appends a rectangle to the path.
description: The rectangle with rounded corners can be achieved by setting non-zero values to `rx` and `ry` arguments. The `rx` and `ry` values specify the radii of the ellipse defining the rounding of the corners.
The position of the rectangle is specified by the coordinates of its upper-left corner - `x` and `y` arguments.
The rectangle is treated as a new sub-path - it is not connected with the previous sub-path.
The value of the current point is set to (`x` + `w`, `y` + `ry`) - in case `ry` is greater than `h`/2 the current point is set to (`x` + `w`, `y` + `h`/2).

params.name: x
params.description: The horizontal coordinate of the upper-left corner of the rectangle.

params.name: y
params.description: The vertical coordinate of the upper-left corner of the rectangle.

params.name: w
params.description: The width of the rectangle.

params.name: h
params.description: The height of the rectangle.

params.name: rx
params.description: The x-axis radius of the ellipse defining the rounded corners of the rectangle.

params.name: ry
params.description: The y-axis radius of the ellipse defining the rounded corners of the rectangle.

params.name: cw
params.description: Specifies the path direction: `true` for clockwise, `false` for counterclockwise.

notes: For `rx` and `ry` greater than or equal to the half of `w` and the half of `h`, respectively, the shape become an ellipse.

members.name: appendCircle
members.signature: Result appendCircle(float cx, float cy, float rx, float ry, bool cw = true) noexcept
members.brief: Appends an ellipse to the path.
description: The position of the ellipse is specified by the coordinates of its center - `cx` and `cy` arguments.
The ellipse is treated as a new sub-path - it is not connected with the previous sub-path.
The value of the current point is set to (`cx`, `cy` - `ry`).

params.name: cx
params.description: The horizontal coordinate of the center of the ellipse.

params.name: cy
params.description: The vertical coordinate of the center of the ellipse.

params.name: rx
params.description: The x-axis radius of the ellipse.

params.name: ry
params.description: The y-axis radius of the ellipse.

params.name: cw
params.description: Specifies the path direction: `true` for clockwise, `false` for counterclockwise.

members.name: appendPath
members.signature: Result appendPath(const PathCommand* cmds, uint32_t cmdCnt, const Point* pts, uint32_t ptsCnt) noexcept
members.brief: Appends a given sub-path to the path.
description: The current point value is set to the last point from the sub-path. For each command from the `cmds` array, an appropriate number of points in `pts` array should be specified. If the number of points in the `pts` array is different than the number required by the `cmds` array, the shape with this sub-path will not be displayed on the screen.

params.name: cmds
params.description: The array of the commands in the sub-path.

params.name: cmdCnt
params.description: The number of the sub-path's commands.

params.name: pts
params.description: The array of the two-dimensional points.

params.name: ptsCnt
params.description: The number of the points in the `pts` array.

notes: The interface is designed for optimal path setting if the caller has a completed path commands already.

members.name: strokeWidth
members.brief: Sets the stroke width for the path.
description: This function defines the thickness of the stroke applied to all figures in the path object. A stroke is the outline drawn along the edges of the path's geometry.

params.name: width
params.description: The width of the stroke in pixels. Must be positive value. (The initial value is 0)

notes: A value of `width` 0 disables the stroke.

members.name: strokeFill
members.signature: Result strokeFill(uint8_t r, uint8_t g, uint8_t b, uint8_t a = 255) noexcept
members.brief: Sets the stroke color for the path.
description: This function defines the RGBA color of the stroke applied to all figures in the path object. The stroke color is used when rendering the outline of the path geometry.

params.name: r
params.description: The red color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255]. The initial value is 0.

params.name: g
params.description: The green color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255]. The initial value is 0.

params.name: b
params.description: The blue color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255]. The initial value is 0.

params.name: a
params.description: The alpha channel value in the range [0 ~ 255], where 0 is completely transparent and 255 is opaque. The initial value is 0.

notes: If the stroke width is 0 (initial value), the stroke will not be visible regardless of the color.
Either a solid color or a gradient fill is applied, depending on what was set as last.

members.name: strokeFill
members.brief: Sets the gradient fill of the stroke for all of the figures from the path.

params.name: f
params.description: The gradient fill.

retvals.description: In case a `nullptr` is passed as the argument.

notes: If the stroke width is 0 (initial value), the stroke will not be visible regardless of the color.
Either a solid color or a gradient fill is applied, depending on what was set as last.

members.name: strokeDash
members.signature: Result strokeDash(const float* dashPattern, uint32_t cnt, float offset = 0.0f) noexcept
members.brief: Sets the dash pattern of the stroke.

params.name: dashPattern
params.description: An array of alternating dash and gap lengths.

params.name: cnt
params.description: The length of the `dashPattern` array.

params.name: offset
params.description: The shift of the starting point within the repeating dash pattern, from which the pattern begins to be applied.

retvals.description: In case `dashPattern` is `nullptr` and `cnt` > 0 or `dashPattern` is not `nullptr` and `cnt` is zero.

notes: To reset the stroke dash pattern, pass `nullptr` to `dashPattern` and zero to `cnt`.
Values of `dashPattern` less than zero are treated as zero.
If all values in the `dashPattern` are equal to or less than 0, the dash is ignored.
If the `dashPattern` contains an odd number of elements, the sequence is repeated in the same order to form an even-length pattern, preserving the alternation of dashes and gaps.

members.name: strokeCap
members.brief: Sets the cap style of the stroke in the open sub-paths.

params.name: cap
params.description: The cap style value. The initial value is `StrokeCap::Square`.

members.name: strokeJoin
members.brief: Sets the join style for stroked path segments.
description: The join style is used for joining the two line segment while stroking the path.

params.name: join
params.description: The join style value. The initial value is `StrokeJoin::Bevel`.

members.name: strokeMiterlimit
members.brief: Sets the stroke miterlimit.

params.name: miterlimit
params.description: The miterlimit imposes a limit on the extent of the stroke join, when the `StrokeJoin::Miter` join style is set. The initial value is 4.

members.name: trimpath
members.signature: Result trimpath(float begin, float end, bool simultaneous = true) noexcept
members.brief: Sets the trim of the shape along the defined path segment, allowing control over which part of the shape is visible.
description: If the values of the arguments `begin` and `end` exceed the 0-1 range, they are wrapped around in a manner similar to angle wrapping, effectively treating the range as circular.

params.name: begin
params.description: Specifies the start of the segment to display along the path.

params.name: end
params.description: Specifies the end of the segment to display along the path.

params.name: simultaneous
params.description: Determines how to trim multiple paths within a single shape. If set to `true` (default), trimming is applied simultaneously to all paths; Otherwise, all paths are treated as a single entity with a combined length equal to the sum of their individual lengths and are trimmed as such.

members.name: fill
members.signature: Result fill(uint8_t r, uint8_t g, uint8_t b, uint8_t a = 255) noexcept
members.brief: Sets the solid color for all of the figures from the path.
description: The parts of the shape defined as inner are colored.

params.name: r
params.description: The red color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255]. The initial value is 0.

params.name: g
params.description: The green color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255]. The initial value is 0.

params.name: b
params.description: The blue color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255]. The initial value is 0.

params.name: a
params.description: The alpha channel value in the range [0 ~ 255], where 0 is completely transparent and 255 is opaque. The initial value is 0.

notes: Either a solid color or a gradient fill is applied, depending on what was set as last.

members.name: fill
members.brief: Sets the gradient fill for all of the figures from the path.
description: The parts of the shape defined as inner are filled.

params.name: f
params.description: The unique pointer to the gradient fill.

notes: Either a solid color or a gradient fill is applied, depending on what was set as last.

members.name: fillRule
members.brief: Sets the fill rule for the shape.
description: Specifies how the interior of the shape is determined when its path intersects itself. The initial fill rule is `FillRule::NonZero`.

params.name: r
params.description: The fill rule to apply to the shape.

members.name: order
members.brief: Sets the rendering order of the stroke and the fill.

params.name: strokeFirst
params.description: If `true` the stroke is rendered before the fill, otherwise the stroke is rendered as the second one (the initial option).

members.name: path
members.signature: Result path(const PathCommand** cmds, uint32_t* cmdsCnt, const Point** pts, uint32_t* ptsCnt) const noexcept
members.brief: Retrieves the current path data of the shape.
description: This function provides access to the shape's path data, including the commands and points that define the path.

params.name: cmds
params.description: Pointer to the array of commands representing the path. Can be `nullptr` if this information is not needed.

params.name: cmdsCnt
params.description: Pointer to the variable that receives the number of commands in the `cmds` array. Can be `nullptr` if this information is not needed.

params.name: pts
params.description: Pointer to the array of two-dimensional points that define the path. Can be `nullptr` if this information is not needed.

params.name: ptsCnt
params.description: Pointer to the variable that receives the number of points in the `pts` array. Can be `nullptr` if this information is not needed.

members.name: fill
members.brief: Gets the pointer to the gradient fill of the shape.
members.returns: The pointer to the gradient fill of the stroke when succeed, `nullptr` in case no fill was set.

members.name: fill
members.signature: Result fill(uint8_t* r, uint8_t* g, uint8_t* b, uint8_t* a = nullptr) const noexcept
members.brief: Gets the solid color of the shape.

params.name: r
params.description: The red color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255].

params.name: g
params.description: The green color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255].

params.name: b
params.description: The blue color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255].

params.name: a
params.description: The alpha channel value in the range [0 ~ 255], where 0 is completely transparent and 255 is opaque.

members.name: fillRule
members.brief: Retrieves the current fill rule used by the shape.
description: This function returns the fill rule, which determines how the interior regions of the shape are calculated when it overlaps itself.
members.returns: The current FillRule value of the shape.

members.name: strokeWidth
members.brief: Gets the stroke width.
members.returns: The stroke width value when succeed, zero if no stroke was set.

members.name: strokeFill
members.signature: Result strokeFill(uint8_t* r, uint8_t* g, uint8_t* b, uint8_t* a = nullptr) const noexcept
members.brief: Gets the color of the shape's stroke.

params.name: r
params.description: The red color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255].

params.name: g
params.description: The green color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255].

params.name: b
params.description: The blue color channel value in the range [0 ~ 255].

params.name: a
params.description: The alpha channel value in the range [0 ~ 255], where 0 is completely transparent and 255 is opaque.

members.name: strokeFill
members.brief: Gets the pointer to the gradient fill of the stroke.
members.returns: The pointer to the gradient fill of the stroke when succeed, `nullptr` otherwise.

members.name: strokeDash
members.signature: uint32_t strokeDash(const float** dashPattern, float* offset = nullptr) const noexcept
members.brief: Gets the dash pattern of the stroke.

params.name: dashPattern
params.description: The pointer to the memory, where the dash pattern array is stored.

params.name: offset
params.description: The shift of the starting point within the repeating dash pattern.

members.name: strokeCap
members.brief: Gets the cap style used for stroking the path.
members.returns: The cap style value of the stroke.

members.name: strokeJoin
members.brief: Gets the join style value used for stroking the path.
members.returns: The join style value of the stroke.

members.name: strokeMiterlimit
members.brief: Gets the stroke miterlimit.
members.returns: The stroke miterlimit value when succeed, 4 if no stroke was set.

members.name: gen
members.brief: Creates a new Shape object.
description: This function allocates and returns a new Shape instance. To properly destroy the Shape object, use Paint::rel().
members.returns: A pointer to the newly created Shape object.

members.name: type
members.brief: Returns the ID value of this class.
description: This method can be used to check the current concrete instance type.
members.returns: The class type ID of the Shape instance.
